content: Pramoxine is a medication prescribed to temporarily alleviate pain and itching caused by insect bites, contact with poison ivy, poison oak, or poison sumac, minor cuts, scrapes, burns, minor skin irritations, rashes, or dry, itchy skin. It is also used to relieve soreness, burning, itching, and pain associated with hemorrhoids and other minor rectal irritations or itching. Pramoxine belongs to a class of medications known as topical anesthetics, which work by blocking nerve signals that transmit pain. Pramoxine is available as a gel or spray for application to the skin. It is typically applied to the affected area several times a day. For hemorrhoidal cream, lotion, or foam, it may be applied after bowel movements as needed or as directed by a healthcare provider. Always follow the instructions provided on the package or prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use pramoxine exactly as directed, and do not use more or less of it, or for a longer duration than prescribed. If symptoms persist for more than seven days, worsen, or resolve and then return, discontinue use and contact your doctor. Avoid getting pramoxine in your eyes or nose. If it accidentally enters your eyes, rinse them thoroughly with water and contact your doctor. Do not apply pramoxine to open wounds, damaged or blistered skin, deep wounds, or large areas of skin. Unless instructed by your doctor, do not use bandages or wraps over the treated area. Do not insert moistened medication pads, cream, gel, or foam into the rectum using your fingers or any device. To use pramoxine cream, gel, spray, or lotion, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands. 2. Clean the affected area with mild soap and warm water, then rinse thoroughly. 3. Pat the area dry with a clean, soft cloth or tissue. 4. Apply a small amount of pramoxine to the affected area. 5. Wash your hands thoroughly after application. To use pramoxine pledgets: 1. Wash your hands. 2. Clean the affected rectal area with mild soap and warm water, then rinse thoroughly. 3. Gently pat the area dry with a clean, soft cloth or tissue. 4. Open the sealed pouch and remove the pledget. 5. Apply the medication from the pledget to the affected rectal area by patting. If needed, fold the pledget and leave it in place for up to 15 minutes. 6. Remove the pledget and dispose of it out of reach of children. 7. Wash your hands thoroughly. To use pramoxine hemorrhoidal foam: 1. Wash your hands. 2. Clean the affected area with mild soap and warm water, then rinse thoroughly. 3. Gently pat the area dry with a clean, soft cloth or tissue. 4. Shake the foam container. 5. Squirt a small amount of foam onto a clean tissue and apply it to the affected rectal area. 6. Wash your hands thoroughly after application. Pramoxine may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using pramoxine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to pramoxine, other topical anesthetics, or any other medications. Also, disclose any other prescription or nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, or herbal products you are using. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using pramoxine, contact your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Pramoxine may cause side effects. Mild side effects include redness, irritation, swelling, burning, stinging, pain, or dryness at the application site. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, may include bleeding at the application site, hives, skin rash, severe itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, and hoarseness. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while using this medication to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store pramoxine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Keep aerosol containers, sprays, or lotions away from fire, flames, or extreme heat. Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and do not incinerate aerosol containers. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. If you have any questions about pramoxine, consult your doctor or pharmacist.
